The client finds and runs the operations of the store's Web API and GraphQL schema, as the admin user or integration it authenticates with. What it does Serves MCP over HTTP at POST /rest/all/V1/mcp , on Magento's REST stack. Magento authenticates the caller and checks the ACL. Serves MCP over standard input and output (stdio) for a client that runs on the same machine as the store, with bin/magento hryvinskyi:mcp:serve . The client acts as an admin user you name. Turns every service method that a webapi.xml route calls into an ability , for example catalog.product_repository.get_list . A store has about 600 of them. Turns every query field of the store's GraphQL schema into an ability that runs as a guest. Mutation fields are an option. Lets another module register its own abilities in di.xml . Shows the client three tools only: discover_abilities , get_ability_info and execute_ability . The client searches the abilities and runs one by name. Tells the client, when it connects, that timestamps such as created_at are UTC and which time zone the store runs in, so a day the user names is filtered on in UTC. Lets the client keep only the fields of a result it needs ( fields of execute_ability ), so a list of products or orders stays small. Blocks abilities that change data until you allow them (read-only mode), keeps abilities that any guest may call off until you allow them, asks for confirmation on abilities you mark, and always refuses a built-in list of dangerous ones. Keeps client sessions in the database. Shows the server on Stores › Settings › MCP Server : its state, how a client connects (a Claude Desktop extension to download, links for Cursor and VS Code, a Claude Code command, and a configuration to copy for each client), and every ability with its exposure and why. You put abilities on the deny-list or ask for confirmation there, one by one or many at once. The page under Stores › MCP Server lists the store's sections, the areas of the admin panel, each with its abilities and a switch: Requirements PHP 8.1 or higher, with the zlib extension Magento 2.4.x (Open Source or Adobe Commerce) The admin UI kit hryvinskyi/magento2-admin-ui (module Hryvinskyi_AdminUi ), which carries the look and typeface of the MCP Server page. Composer installs it with this module. Installation Via Composer (recommended) composer require hryvinskyi/magento2-mcp-server bin/magento module:enable Hryvinskyi_McpServer bin/magento setup:upgrade bin/magento cache:flush Manual Installation Download the module from GitHub. Place it in app/code/Hryvinskyi/McpServer . Run: bin/magento module:enable Hryvinskyi_McpServer bin/magento setup:upgrade bin/magento cache:flush setup:upgrade creates three tables: hryvinskyi_mcp_session , hryvinskyi_mcp_confirmation and hryvinskyi_mcp_ability_override . When you upgrade a store that runs an older version, also run bin/magento setup:upgrade : the module now needs Hryvinskyi_AdminUi , and Magento enables a new module there. On Magento 2.4.9 a new admin controller is found only after bin/magento cache:clean compiled_config (or cache:flush ), because the list of admin actions is cached under that cache type. Until then the page's integration picker gets a 404 and says the token could not be fetched. Configuration Go to Stores > Configuration > MCP Server > MCP Server . All options are set in the default scope only. Group General : Option Description Default Enable MCP Server While it is off, the endpoint refuses every message No Read-only Mode Clients may only call abilities that read data. Abilities that write or delete are blocked Yes Expose Anonymous Abilities Lets clients call abilities that any guest may call through the REST API, such as account creation or guest checkout. Through MCP, the CAPTCHA and rate limits set for each REST route do not apply, so these abilities are denied while this is No. Yes also lets every GraphQL ability run, because they all run as a guest. To keep them off, set Enable GraphQL Abilities to No No The server is off after install. Turning it on is your step. Group Personal Data (see Personal data ): Option Path Description Default Hide Personal Data hryvinskyi_mcp_server/personal_data/hide Every value under a personal field reaches the client as [personal data] . No sends results as they are Yes Personal Data Fields hryvinskyi_mcp_server/personal_data/fields One field name per line; * stands for any characters Email, names and name prefix/suffix, phone, fax, street, postcode, city, date of birth, tax/VAT number, gender, company, customer note, IP addresses, the card holder and the card's last digits, payment additional information, gift message sender, recipient and text, shipping labels Group GraphQL : Option Path Description Default Enable GraphQL Abilities hryvinskyi_mcp_server/graphql/enabled Offers the query fields of the store's GraphQL schema as abilities. They are still denied until Expose Anonymous Abilities is Yes Yes Expose GraphQL Mutations hryvinskyi_mcp_server/graphql/expose_mutations Also offers the mutation fields as abilities. Mutations write data, so read-only mode blocks them No GraphQL Endpoint URL hryvinskyi_mcp_server/graphql/endpoint_url An absolute http(s) URL ending in /graphql , for a server that cannot reach its own public host name. Empty means the secure base URL of the store view below, followed by graphql . That default is refused, and no GraphQL ability is listed, when the stored base URL is a placeholder such as {{base_url}} : Magento fills it in from the host of each request. Set this URL then Empty Store View hryvinskyi_mcp_server/graphql/store_code The store view the GraphQL abilities run in, sent as the Store header. Empty means the default store view Empty See GraphQL abilities for what these settings do. Calling the endpoint The URL is https://<host>/rest/all/V1/mcp . Use POST with a JSON-RPC 2.0 body. Send Content-Type: application/json . The store code must be all . /rest/V1/mcp and /rest/default/V1/mcp answer HTTP 400, because they would run abilities in a store view's scope. Send Authorization: Bearer <token> with every request. Serve the endpoint over HTTPS only. The token is a credential, and every answer can hold store data. A caller who is not authenticated, or whose role lacks Use the MCP endpoint , gets Magento's own 401 answer. While the server is disabled, the answer is HTTP 403 with JSON-RPC error -32001 . Tokens Integration token (recommended). Go to System > Extensions > Integrations and add an integration. On its API tab, give it the resource Use the MCP endpoint , plus whatever resources the abilities it will run need. Activate the integration and copy its Access Token . Magento accepts an integration's access token as a Bearer token only when Stores > Configuration > Services > OAuth > Consumer Settings > Allow OAuth Access Tokens to be used as standalone Bearer tokens is Yes . It is off by default ( oauth/consumer/enable_integration_as_bearer ). Admin token. POST /rest/V1/integration/admin/token returns a token for an admin user. It expires after Admin Token Lifetime (hours) ( oauth/access_token_lifetime/admin , default 4). With two-factor authentication enabled, that endpoint refuses to issue a token. Use an integration instead. Connecting a client The page Stores › Settings › MCP Server has a Connection card and an Install card. It needs the resource View the MCP Server page . Create an integration first (see Tokens ). Picking the token. The Integration list on the Connection card holds every integration of the store. A ready one (active, allowed Use the MCP endpoint or all resources, with an access token that is not revoked) fills its access token into the Access token field when you pick it. The page does not print tokens: the browser fetches the one you pick from the store, with a POST that carries the form key, and the answer is not cached. This needs the resource System Integrations ( Magento_Integration::integrations ), the one Magento asks for before it shows a token on its own integration page, besides View the MCP Server page . An integration that is not ready shows why, with a link to its edit page, and its token is never served. New integration opens Magento's own form in a new tab. Without System Integrations the list is not shown, and you paste the token. Bearer setting. While Magento does not accept integration tokens as Bearer tokens (see step 4 of Tokens ), the Connection card shows a warning, because the store refuses every client that sends one. It links to the OAuth settings when you may open them ( Magento_Integration::config_oauth ). Pasting a token. Picking is optional. You can paste a token by hand, for an integration the list does not offer or when you may not pick. Typing in the field puts the list back on Paste a token by hand . The field never shows a token while the list names an integration it did not come from: Picking an integration empties the field first, whatever it held, typed or picked, and only then fetches that integration's token. A pick that is refused, fails or is not ready leaves the field empty. Choosing Paste a token by hand empties the field only when it holds a picked token. A token you typed stays. A token the field lost to a pick does not come back. Paste it again. The card says This integration's token cannot be used only when the store refuses that integration. Any other problem, such as no answer, an error page or a missing right, reads as The token could not be fetched . Claude Desktop. Download the .mcpb file with Download for Claude Desktop (.mcpb) and open it. Claude Desktop asks for the store endpoint, already filled in, and for the access token. It keeps the token in the system's keychain. The extension is not signed, so Claude Desktop warns before it installs it. The extension runs on the Node.js that ships with Claude Desktop. You install nothing else. The extension is named after the store's host. Several stores can be installed side by side. The extension has its own version. After an upgrade of this module that changes it, download the file again and open it. The extension refuses an http:// endpoint, unless the host is localhost , 127.0.0.1 or [::1] . A store without a secure base URL needs one before you use it. It never follows a redirect and never retries a request, because a call may change data. A lost session is opened again once. If your organisation blocks custom extensions in Claude Desktop, use the manual configuration with mcp-remote below. Cursor and VS Code. Pick an integration, or paste the access token, into the field Access token on the page. A picked token comes from the store; a pasted one stays in the browser tab and is never sent to the store. When the field holds a valid token, the links Add to Cursor and Install in VS Code appear. They open the client, which asks you to confirm. The token is then part of the client's own configuration file, in plain text. Claude Code. The page shows this command with a button to copy it, with your token in it once the field holds one: claude mcp add --transport http magento " https://<host>/rest/all/V1/mcp " --header " Authorization: Bearer <token> " The shell keeps the command, token included, in its history. To keep the token out of the history, run claude mcp add without --header and add the header to the configuration file it writes. Until the field holds a token, the command and the JSON configurations show the placeholder <integration-token> . Client configuration Each client's configuration by hand. Claude Desktop uses this when the extension is blocked. Cursor ( .cursor/mcp.json , a remote server with headers): { "mcpServers" : { "magento" : { "url" : " https://<host>/rest/all/V1/mcp " , "headers" : { "Authorization" : " Bearer <token> " }}}} Claude Desktop ( claude_desktop_config.json ) starts local commands only. A remote server with a Bearer header goes through the mcp-remote bridge, which needs Node.js. Keep Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER} without a space, as mcp-remote documents: { "mcpServers" : { "magento" : { "command" : " npx " , "args" : [ " mcp-remote " , " https://<host>/rest/all/V1/mcp " , " --header " , " Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER} " ], "env" : { "AUTH_HEADER" : " Bearer <token> " }}}} Protocol The transport is Streamable HTTP with JSON responses. There is no event stream. The first message must be initialize . The answer carries the session id in the Mcp-Session-Id header. Send that header with every later message, notifications included. A missing header is HTTP 400. An unknown, expired or foreign session is HTTP 404. The client then sends initialize again. Supported protocol versions: 2025-11-25 , 2025-06-18 , 2025-03-26 , 2024-11-05 . initialize answers with the client's version when it is supported, else with the newest. A later MCP-Protocol-Version header must name the version the session negotiated, or the request gets HTTP 400. Supported methods: initialize , notifications/initialized , ping , tools/list and tools/call . Any other method is JSON-RPC error -32601 . Batches are accepted. initialize must be sent alone. In a batch, it gets the error -32600 for its own element. A notification or a client response gets HTTP 202 with no body. Only notifications/initialized does anything as a notification. A request method sent without an id , tools/call included, runs nothing. GET answers HTTP 405 with Allow: POST, DELETE . DELETE with the session id ends that session (HTTP 204). A request with an Origin header is refused with HTTP 403 unless the header names a host of one of the store's base URLs. Sessions A session is stored in the hryvinskyi_mcp_session table. It belongs to the caller who opened it. Any other caller who sends its id gets 404. A session expires 24 hours after its last use. The cron job hryvinskyi_mcp_session_cleanup runs every hour and removes expired sessions. A caller holds at most 20 live sessions, stdio sessions included. When the caller opens one more, the sessions that were used least recently are ended. A client that gets HTTP 404 for its session opens a new one with initialize . Flushing caches does not end sessions. Limits Limit Value Answer when it is exceeded Request body 1 MB (1048576 bytes) HTTP 400, error -32600 , id: null Messages in a batch 20 HTTP 400, error -32600 , id: null JSON nesting depth 64 levels HTTP 400, error -32600 , id: null Live sessions per caller 20 The least recently used sessions are ended A developer can change the body size, the batch size and the session count in etc/di.xml : the arguments maxBodyBytes of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Protocol\Server , maxBatchSize of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Protocol\MessageParser and maxSessionsPerCaller of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Session\DbSessionStore . The nesting depth is fixed. Using stdio For a client that runs on the same machine as the store, and starts a command instead of calling a URL. The command acts as an admin user. It needs Magento_User and Magento_Security , which Magento ships with. bin/magento hryvinskyi:mcp:serve --admin-user= < login > The admin user's role needs Use the MCP endpoint , plus whatever resources the abilities it will run need. The server must be enabled. The command reads one JSON-RPC message, or one batch, from each line of standard input. It writes each answer as one line to standard output. Everything else goes to standard error. A line over 1 MB gets the error -32600 and the command goes on. It runs until its input ends, then exits with 0. It exits with 1 and a message on standard error when the --admin-user option is missing, when the admin does not exist, is inactive, is locked or is past the expiry date set on the account, when the role lacks Use the MCP endpoint , when the server is disabled, or when the process already runs in another area. It also exits with 1 when the admin loses access while it runs: the next message stops it. Before it reads any input, it runs one check message. If that fails for any reason, the command stops with exit 1. The command does not check a password or a token. See Privacy and security for what that means. Client configuration Pass display_errors=stderr to PHP, so that a PHP error never lands in the answers. Claude Desktop ( claude_desktop_config.json ): { "mcpServers" : { "magento" : { "command" : " php " , "args" : [ " -d " , " display_errors=stderr " , " <path>/bin/magento " , " hryvinskyi:mcp:serve " , " --admin-user " , " <login> " ]}}} With DDEV, the same command runs in the container. If the client does not start in the project directory, add "-p", "<project>" after "exec" : { "mcpServers" : { "magento" : { "command" : " ddev " , "args" : [ " exec " , " php " , " -d " , " display_errors=stderr " , " bin/magento " , " hryvinskyi:mcp:serve " , " --admin-user " , " <login> " ]}}} How it runs Every line starts a new bin/magento process, which handles that one message and ends. So a changed setting, a changed admin account or role, or a changed override reaches the next message with no restart. The cost is the start of bin/magento for each message: about 0.4 s per message on a development machine. A client that starts a session ( initialize , notifications/initialized , tools/list ) waits a couple of seconds in total. A message process may run for 300 seconds. After that it is stopped, each request on the line gets the error -32603 with its own id , and the command goes on. A notification gets no answer. The same happens when a message process fails in any other way, for example when the database connection drops. The limit is the messageTimeoutSeconds argument of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Stdio\StdioLoop . The command hryvinskyi:mcp:stdio-message is the message process. It is hidden and internal. Do not call it. The session works as over HTTP, and it counts toward the admin's 20 live sessions. When the input ends, the command ends its session. If the client sends initialize again, the command switches to the new session. The earlier one stays until it expires (24 hours without use) or the cap of 20 removes it. When the session has expired (24 hours without use) or the cap of 20 has ended it, the command opens a new one by sending the client's own initialize again, and notifications/initialized if the client sent it. Then it sends the message again, once. If that fails, the client gets the session's not-found error. Restart the client then. Web API routes that webapi.xml marks as secure run over stdio, because a local pipe counts as a secure channel. The three tools Abilities are not listed as tools. A client finds one, reads its arguments, then runs it. discover_abilities Searches the abilities. All arguments are optional. Argument Description query Words to find in the ability name, title or category. The search is case-insensitive. Empty lists every ability category Only abilities of this category: a Magento module name, for example Magento_Catalog , or GraphQL access read , write or delete limit 1 to 100. Default 25 offset 0 or more. Default 0 The answer is {total, abilities: [{name, title, category, access, exposure}]} , sorted by name. Every ability is listed, whatever the caller's role allows. get_ability_info Takes name . The answer is {name, title, description, category, source, access, aclResources, exposure, allowedForYou, inputSchema} , plus denialReason when no client may call the ability: deny_list , read_only_mode , anonymous_ability or another rule's code. inputSchema is a JSON Schema built from Magento's Web API metadata. Data types nest at most six levels in it. allowedForYou tells whether the caller's role holds every resource in aclResources . execute_ability Runs an ability. Argument Description name The ability name. Required arguments An object keyed by argument name, as inputSchema describes. Default {} confirmationToken The token that the -32004 error of this same call carried, sent once the user confirmed. Optional fields Only these fields of the result, each a dot-separated path, for example ["items.sku", "items.price", "total_count"] . A path through a list keeps that field of every element. Optional; without it the whole result comes back The old confirm argument is gone. A call that sends it gets a tool error that explains the token. On success, the tool result holds the value once, as JSON text in its first content item. There is no structuredContent : the tools declare no output schema, and every client reads the text. With fields , the value keeps only the fields named. A field the result does not have is not an error, because the ability has already run: a note after the value in content names it and lists the fields found where the path left the result. A path with an empty name, such as items..sku , is refused before the ability runs. Case Answer Unknown ability, or arguments the service cannot take A tool result with isError: true and a message, so the model can correct itself The service fails A tool result with isError: true . A message meant for users is passed on. Any other error is masked and logged Denied JSON-RPC error -32003 , with data: {ability, reason} . See the reasons below The ability needs a confirmation and the call has no valid token JSON-RPC error -32004 , with data: {ability, confirmationToken} . Ask the user, then call again with the same name and arguments plus that token The ability must be called over HTTPS and the request was not A tool result with isError: true The reasons of a -32003 error: Reason Why the call was denied deny_list The ability is on the built-in deny-list or has the deny override read_only_mode Read-only mode is on and the ability writes or deletes anonymous_ability The ability is open to guests and Expose Anonymous Abilities is No acl The caller's role lacks an ACL resource of the ability argument_guard A guard refused the arguments of this call A module that adds an exposure rule can report a reason of its own (see Extending). Confirmation tokens An ability with the confirm override does not run on the first call. The error -32004 carries a confirmationToken . The client asks the user, then calls execute_ability again with the same name and arguments and that token. A token works once and for 10 minutes. It works only for the session that got it, the same caller, the same ability and the same arguments. The order of the keys in arguments does not matter. The token is spent when it is sent, even when the call does not match it. The call then gets a new -32004 error with a new token. An unknown, expired or spent token counts as no token. The cron job hryvinskyi_mcp_session_cleanup also removes expired tokens. A token proves that the client made a second, explicit call for exactly these arguments. It does not prove that a person approved the call. A client that sends the token on its own, with no question to the user, gets the same result. JSON-RPC errors that answer a parsed request come with HTTP 200 and the request's id . Input that cannot be parsed ( -32700 , or an invalid envelope -32600 ) is HTTP 400 with id: null . Abilities Abilities come from three sources: the modules that register them in di.xml (source pool ), the Web API ( webapi ) and the GraphQL schema ( graphql ). get_ability_info names the source. This section is about the Web API abilities; the others have their own sections below. A Web API ability is one service method that a webapi.xml route calls. The name is <module>.<service>.<method> , in snake case. The module part of a Magento module is its name ( catalog ). Another vendor's module has its vendor in front ( acme_gallery ). When several routes call one method, the route with the fewest forced parameters is used. Routes that need the self resource (a customer acting for themselves) are not abilities. A route that webapi.xml marks as secure gives an ability that refuses a request that did not come over HTTPS. The refusal is a tool error. A route whose URL holds an id that the method does not take as a parameter, such as PUT /V1/orders/:parent_id on save , gives an ability with that id as an optional top-level argument. It selects the record to update, as in REST. The module's own endpoint is not an ability. The category is the Magento module name, for example Magento_Catalog . The access comes from the route's HTTP method: GET is read , POST and PUT are write , DELETE is delete . A developer can set the access of one ability by name in etc/di.xml , in the accessOverrides argument of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Source\Webapi\RouteAbilityBuilder . Use it for a GET route that changes data. The array ships empty. A value other than read , write or delete drops the ability and writes a warning to the log. An ability runs the same way a REST call does, with the caller's permissions. The caller needs every ACL resource of the route. If a route cannot become an ability (its name is invalid or taken), it is skipped and a warning goes to the log. The other abilities are not affected. The input schemas are cached in the MCP Server cache type. Cleaning or flushing that cache type rebuilds them. GraphQL abilities Every query field of the store's GraphQL schema is an ability. The module reads the schema by introspection, from the store's own /graphql . The name is graphql.query.<field in snake case> , for example graphql.query.products . A mutation is graphql.mutation.<field> , for example graphql.mutation.create_empty_cart . The category is GraphQL . A query is read access. A mutation is write access, so read-only mode blocks it. graphql.schema.describe_type is a helper. It takes name and describes one type of the schema: its fields with their arguments, its input fields and its enum values. Use it to write a selection or an input object. Who runs them Every GraphQL ability runs as a guest, whoever the MCP caller is. The server sends the call to its own /graphql with no Authorization header and no cookies. It runs in the store view that Store View names, sent as the Store header. With no value, it is the default store view. Their only ACL resource is anonymous . So they follow the rule for anonymous abilities: every GraphQL ability is denied until Expose Anonymous Abilities is Yes. Mutations are also listed only when Expose GraphQL Mutations is Yes. The mutations whose name holds "token", such as those that issue or revoke a customer token or delete a stored payment token, and those that set or reset a password, are always denied. They match the patterns graphql.mutation.*token* and graphql.mutation.*password* of the built-in deny-list. Six query fields answer only a signed-in customer, so a guest always gets a 401 from them. They are not listed: customer , customerCart , customerDownloadableProducts , customerOrders , customerPaymentTokens and wishlist . The excludedFields argument of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Source\GraphQl\GraphQlAbilitySource in di.xml holds the list. Calling one inputSchema has one property for each argument of the field. A field whose result is an object, an interface, a union or a list of them also takes a required selection . It is the selection set of the result: { "name" : " graphql.query.products " , "arguments" : { "search" : " bag " , "selection" : " { items { sku name } } " }} selection is exactly one group in braces. Nothing may follow its closing brace, and # comments are refused. Fields, aliases, arguments, fragments and directives inside the group are checked by the GraphQL server. A field whose result is a scalar or an enum value takes no selection . Setup The server must be able to call its own /graphql . The default URL is the secure base URL of the store view, followed by graphql . If that host name does not resolve from the server itself, set GraphQL Endpoint URL . It accepts only an absolute http(s) URL ending in /graphql . Introspection must be allowed. If app/etc/env.php sets graphql/disable_introspection , the schema cannot be read, and no GraphQL ability is listed. Each GraphQL call holds one PHP-FPM worker, and the loopback request is served by another one. Keep pm.max_children above the number of MCP clients that may call at the same time. The loopback request times out after 30 seconds. The schema is cached in the MCP Server cache type. Clean it after you install a module that changes the GraphQL schema: bin/magento cache:clean hryvinskyi_mcp . A failed read of the schema is remembered for five minutes. The module enables the MCP Server cache type once, on the first setup:upgrade that installs version 1.1.0, because setup:upgrade leaves a newly added cache type disabled. While the type is disabled, every MCP request and every stdio message reads the whole GraphQL schema again, several MB through the loopback. Keep it enabled, or set Enable GraphQL Abilities to No. To turn it back on: bin/magento cache:enable hryvinskyi_mcp . Exposure Every ability has one exposure. When several rules apply, the strictest wins, in this order: Order Exposure When 1 denied The ability is on the built-in deny-list, has the deny override, belongs to a section that is switched off, or is open to guests while Expose Anonymous Abilities is No 2 read_only_blocked Read-only mode is on and the ability is write or delete 3 needs_confirmation The ability has the confirm override 4 exposed None of the above A call that is denied changes nothing. The exposure, the caller's ACL, the confirmation and the argument guards are all checked before the ability runs. Read-only mode It is on after install. Turn it off in the configuration to let clients run abilities that write or delete. Do this only with a token whose role holds just the resources you want a client to use. Built-in deny-list These abilities are always denied, whatever the overrides say: Pattern What it covers integration.* Integrations, and the services that issue admin and customer tokens jwt_user_token.* JWT user tokens two_factor_auth.* Two-factor authentication, including its token endpoints login_as_customer*.* Login as customer customer.account_management.*password* Customer password reset and change graphql.mutation.*token* GraphQL mutations that issue, revoke, exchange or delete a token, such as a customer token or a stored payment token graphql.mutation.*password* GraphQL mutations that set, change or reset a password The patterns are fnmatch patterns in etc/di.xml , in the patterns argument of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Exposure\Rule\BuiltInDenyListRule . Another module can add patterns there. The list cannot be changed in the configuration. Overrides A per-ability override is a row in hryvinskyi_mcp_ability_override : ability , deny and confirm . Overrides only add restrictions. They cannot lift read-only mode or the built-in deny-list. The Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Api\AbilityOverrideRepositoryInterface reads and saves overrides; the MCP Server page edits them (see The admin page ). Sections A section is an area of the admin panel, read from the ACL tree: the nodes right below the root (Catalog, Sales, Customers, Carts, Marketing, Content, System…). Stores holds unrelated areas, so each of its children is a section of its own: Stores › Settings, Stores › Inventory, Stores › Attributes and so on. An ability belongs to the sections of the ACL resources it needs. A module that extends an area with that area's resources lands in its section: product types, configurable and bundle products, stock in Catalog; gift messages in Sales. Resources outside the tree have sections of their own: anonymous is Open to anyone , self is The caller's own account . An ability that needs no resource, or only resources no tree holds, is in Other . The MCP Server page lists every section with its modules, its abilities and how many of them clients may call, and a switch. While a section is off, its abilities are denied with the reason section_off ; an ability in several sections is denied when one of them is off. The switches are rows of hryvinskyi_mcp_section_off , behind Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Api\SectionSwitchesInterface . The areas split like Stores are the split argument of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\Section\AbilitySections in di.xml . Anonymous abilities An ability whose only ACL resource is anonymous can be called by a guest through REST. Through MCP, the CAPTCHA and rate limits of each REST route do not apply. So these abilities are denied with the reason anonymous_ability , until you set Expose Anonymous Abilities to Yes. Turn it on only when you accept that. Every GraphQL ability is one of them. Argument guards A guard looks at the arguments of one call and may refuse it. Guards run after the confirmation check and before the ability runs. A refusal is a -32003 error with the reason argument_guard . The module ships one guard. It refuses customer.customer_repository.save when the arguments hold a passwordHash . Passwords are never set through MCP that way. ACL The caller's role is never used to hide an ability. discover_abilities lists all of them, and get_ability_info says what each needs. The ACL decides only when a call runs. The module adds these ACL resources: Stores > MCP Server ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::mcp_server ) Use the MCP endpoint ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::access ): required to call the endpoint View the MCP Server page ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::view ): the page and its catalog Manage ability exposure ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::manage ): the deny-list, confirmation, section and personal data changes on the page MCP Server Settings ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::config ): the configuration section The admin page Stores › Settings › MCP Server ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::view ): Connection : a card with the endpoint URL (the default store view's secure base URL followed by rest/all/V1/mcp ), the list of integrations to take a token from, New integration , the Access token field and, while integration tokens are not accepted as Bearer tokens, a warning with a link to the OAuth settings (see Connecting a client ). A notice above the cards says so when the server is disabled, when it is in read-only mode, and when some ability sends personal data. Install : the Claude Desktop extension to download, the Add to Cursor and Install in VS Code links, which appear once the token field holds a valid token, and the Claude Code command to copy. A token pasted by hand stays in the browser tab and is never sent to the store; a picked token is fetched from the store. Manual configuration (folded into the Install card): a JSON configuration per client (Claude Desktop, Cursor) and transport (HTTP, stdio), with the file it goes into. The token and the admin login are placeholders you fill in or, once the field holds a token, the token; the page never prints a secret it was not given. Claude Desktop reaches an HTTP server with a Bearer token through the mcp-remote bridge ( npx ). Details (folded): the stdio command, how to authorize, the protocol version, how many abilities a client may call and how many are exposed, and whether personal data is hidden. Sections : every area of the store with its modules and abilities, and a switch for each (see Sections ). Ability catalog : every ability with its source, module, access, required ACL resources and exposure. The exposure line says why: put on the deny-list on this page, on the module's built-in deny-list, open to anyone while anonymous abilities are off, in a section switched off, blocked by read-only mode, or waiting for a confirmation. The section and whether personal data is hidden or shown are columns too. Search and filter by source, module, section, access, exposure and personal data. With Manage ability exposure ( Hryvinskyi_McpServer::manage ): a row puts its ability on the deny-list or takes it off, and the mass actions Add to deny-list , Remove from deny-list , Require confirmation and Clear confirmation , Show personal data and Hide personal data change every selected ability (or every ability the search finds). A change applies to the next call. An ability the module itself keeps denied, or that read-only mode blocks, offers no change: its state does not depend on this page. Extending A source of abilities implements Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Api\AbilitySourceInterface . Add it to the sources argument of Hryvinskyi\McpServer\Model\AbilityCatalog in di.xml . The sources are sorted by their sortOrder attribute: pool is 10, webapi is 20 and graphql is 30. A source without a sortOrder sorts first. When two sources offer one name, the first keeps it.
